title.narrative: Policies & programmes to promote full, productive & decent employment opertationalised

description.narrative: Bangladesh is undergoing a challenging economic transition despite years of sustained growth and poverty reduction. The economy faces high inflation, declining foreign exchange reserves, financial sector vulnerabilities, and impending LDC graduation, while GDP growth slowed to 3.69 per cent in 2024–25. The labour market continues to experience underemployment, informality, skills mismatches, limited workplace-based learning, and weak school-to-work transition systems. These challenges disproportionately affect youth, women, persons with disabilities, returnee migrants, and refugee-affected host communities. While restoring macroeconomic stability remains a priority, the challenge is not only to revive growth but also to strengthen the employment intensity of growth and promote inclusive, productive, and decent employment opportunities. In response, the ILO’s strategy for 2026–2027 will support the Government of Bangladesh in operationalizing an Integrated National Employment Strategy, advancing a pro-employment macroeconomic framework, promoting sectoral diversification, and strengthening integrated employment and skills systems. The ILO will support implementation of the Bangladesh National Qualifications Framework (BNQF), expansion of competency-based and demand-driven training, and scaling up quality apprenticeships and workplace-based learning. Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), digitalized public employment services, Skills Needs Anticipation Services (SNAS), and graduate tracking systems will strengthen labour market efficiency and lifelong learning opportunities. The strategy will also promote safe and regular labour migration through integrated skills preparation, language training, and overseas employment matching systems linked to initiatives including the Bangladesh–EU Talent Partnership. Support will further be provided to revise the National Youth Policy with stronger emphasis on employment creation, entrepreneurship, and youth labour market inclusion
